transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim, Diego Flores (Redwood); Lina Chen, Marcus D'Souza, Priya Nair, Tom Evans (Horizon Edge)

Summary: quick partner intro between Redwood Inference and Horizon Edge to explore cloud/GPU distribution partnership, technical integration points (VPC peering, private deployments), and next steps for a pilot. Discussed security/compliance, SLA expectations, and initial benchmarking plan.

[00:00] Sara (AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time. i'm sara kim from redwood, AE on partnerships. we've got diego from infra, janelle from solutions here too. hi lina, marcus, priya, tom - could you quick intro?
[00:18] Lina (Horizon): sure, hi all. lina chen, head of partnerships at horizon edge. we build edge-optimized cloud regions and offer managed gpu capacity to ISVs and platforms. marcus is our cloud lead.
[00:30] Marcus (Horizon): hey, marcus here. we run both metal and vm-based gpu fleets, focus on latency-sensitive inference near enterprise customers.
[00:40] Diego (SE): awesome. quick agenda — partner intro, what you run today, constraints, integration models (marketplace, bare-metal co-locate, vpc/private), security, then next steps. sound good?
[00:55] Tom (Horizon): yep sounds good.
[01:05] Sara: lina, how do you typically partner — resell, co-sell, or more infra integrations?
[01:15] Lina: we're flexible. for smaller ISVs we resell, for big partners we do co-deployments and managed private deployments. with redwood we were thinking about offering a managed Redwood Dedicated variant on our regions and also referencing Redwood API in our marketplace.
[01:35] Diego: nice. from a technical lens, main integration patterns we see: 1) marketplace listing calling hosted api, 2) dedicated capacity running Redwood runtime as a managed service on your gpu fleet (we call that co-locate), or 3) a private customer deployment with a control plane in redwood and data plane in horizon vpc.
[01:58] Priya (Horizon): for us the private deployment with VPC peering and KMS integration is high interest — many enterprise customers need keys on their side and strict data residency.
[02:12] Sara: ok makes sense. can you share a bit about customer profiles and expected volumes? even rough qps and sequence lengths helps.
[02:24] Marcus: typical request profiles vary — some customers want short chat completions (avg 150 tokens, spikes to 2k), others run long-form summarization (3k-8k tokens). Traffic is bursty, daily peak windows. peak tps per customer in pilot would be 50-200 qps, multi-tenant pool.
[02:50] Diego: noted. for those shapes we usually recommend mixing quantized model variants for cost and a smaller low-latency variant for interactive workloads. curious — are you aiming to surface Redwood as a managed marketplace offering or white-label for your customers?
[03:05] Lina: we'd like both options eventually. initial go-to-market: list a managed Redwood Dedicated product in marketplace, then offer white-label/private for select enterprise accounts.
[03:18] Sara: great. quick security Qs — do you require SOC2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs? what's baseline for your customers?
[03:30] Priya: yes SOC2 is table stakes. SSO/SAML or OIDC, SAML mainly. also audit logs, KMS/HSM for key management; some customers require bring-your-own-key.
[03:44] Diego: Redwood supports SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations — including customer-managed keys. sometimes the transcript system borks product names — but our Redwood Private control plane can be run in your VPC or we do a managed VPC peering model.
[04:00] Marcus: latency SLOs — customers expect 95th percentile under 200ms for short prompts; for longer sequences they accept higher. how do you typically guarantee that on shared pools?
[04:15] Diego: we use smart routing + autoscaling. on Redwood Dedicated we can reserve capacity and configure autoscale/burst policies; prefix caching and continuous batching reduce cold-token latency. the tradeoff is cost vs latency — smaller batch sizes for strict latency increases unit cost.
[04:35] Tom: are there known integrations with your runtime to our orchestration? we run a custom scheduler but support k8s + nomad; we also have orchestration for bare metal.
[04:48] Diego: runtime can run as k8s + helm chart or as a bare-metal managed agent. the kernel selection and scheduler piece is integrated but we expose metrics and tracing hooks for your infra to hook into.
[05:05] [interruption/noise] Speaker 1: sorry — mic glitch.
[05:18] Sara: no worries. on commercial/ops: pricing — how do you usually structure revenue between infra partner and redwood? Lina?
[05:28] Lina: we typically do revenue share for resell and a capacity commit for dedicated. interested in terms around reserved packs + overage. also need an SLA for uptime and latency for marketplace customers.
[05:41] Sara: we can share standard reserved capacity terms and SLA tiers. we'll also share a pilot pricing template.
[05:50] Marcus: technical question — networking: do you support private peering (VPC peering), vpn, or direct connect? and are control plane API calls over the internet or can they be tunneled?
[06:03] Diego: we support VPC peering and private connectivity. control plane can be run in redwood-managed control plane with private connect to your data plane, or a full private control plane option. some customers prefer the latter for audit constraints.
[06:20] Priya: for KMS — if customer wants BYOK, do you support HSM integration?
[06:27] Diego: yes HSM/KMS integrations are supported, we integrate with common providers and offer on-prem connector for HSMs.
[06:35] Lina: another commercial angle — do you have a channel partner program? we want clear enablement materials, support SLAs, and co-selling guidelines.
[06:46] Sara: yes we have a partner program — tiers, deal registration, enablement, and dedicated partner success contacts. we'll share the partner one-pager.
[06:58] [00:07:10] Marcus: benchmarks — have you published any numbers on cost per token and latency for typical models on different GPUs? we need to know how to price our managed offering.
[07:22] Diego: we publish performance profiles in the model catalog (sometimes transcription calls it the 'model cupboard' ha). we'll share per-model latency/cost spreadsheets. for example, a quantized 8-bit variant on A800-like GPUs yields X tokens/sec in our internal tests; we'll provide numbers and a benchmarking template for you to run on your fleet.
[07:45] Priya: we'd like to run a pilot on a small node pool — can you share the benchmark harness so we can run with our images and report back?
[07:55] Diego: yes. action: i'll share the benchmark harness + sample configs.
[08:02] Tom: any legal/compliance blockers for listing on our marketplace? need standard MSSA or SOW templates?
[08:12] Sara: legal will provide MSSA + marketplace terms. also we'll surface security docs (SOC2 report, penetration test summary) — share as link.
[08:24] [00:08:30] Lina: important to flag — some of our enterprise customers will insist on data residency in eu-west. can redwood support regional private deployments?
[08:40] Diego: yes, we support regional private control planes and can pin model versions and configs per region. data residency and audit logs per customer are supported.
[08:52] Marcus: network egress costs — when routing to redwood hosted models, who bears egress? if we do dedicated co-deploy, that reduces egress, right?
[09:04] Sara: correct, co-deploy or private means less cross-cloud egress. we'll include egress considerations in the benchmark/pricing doc.
[09:15] [00:09:20] Priya: any limitations on model types? we plan to support both open models and some 3rd party licensed weights. can you host customer-supplied models?
[09:32] Diego: we onboard open and customer-supplied models. licensing for 3rd-party weights is handled by the customer; we can run the runtime on those weights as long as licensing permits.
[09:45] Tom: what about multi-tenancy isolation? our customers require strong tenant isolation and key separation.
[09:54] Diego: Dedicated pools are isolated, and Private mode gives you per-tenant networking and key separation. we also provide token-level audit logs.
[10:05] Lina: timeline — if we want to go to pilot in 6-8 weeks, is that feasible?
[10:12] Diego: pilot in 6-8 weeks is realistic: share expected traffic profile, we'll propose infra footprint and configs; then we can run a 2-week benchmark and a short pilot.
[10:24] [00:10:30] Sara: ok next steps recap: i'll share partner one-pager, Diego will send benchmark template & harness, horizon to share expected workload and sample data shapes, and we'll schedule a tech deep dive with priya and infra team.
[10:40] Marcus: one more — do you have any references from other cloud partners?
[10:46] Sara: yes, we can share a short list — will include a couple of partner case studies.
[10:54] [00:11:00] Priya: for the technical deep dive, please include our ops lead (name redacted here) and include network folks.
[11:11] Diego: will do. also we'll surface the specifics of kernel optimizations and quantization tradeoffs in that session.
[11:25] [00:11:40] Tom: curious about billing integration — can we surface usage to our billing system?
[11:34] Sara: yes we support billing exports and event webhooks; partner marketplace integrations can pull usage for billing reconciliation.
[11:44] Marcus: any immediate blockers?
[11:48] Lina: none immediate. legal will want to review MSSA templates.
[11:55] Sara: perfect. closing — thanks everyone. we'll send notes and links to security docs, partner one-pager, benchmark harness.
[12:07] Diego: thanks all.
[12:10] [END]
